item.title: AI Coding Governance Concerns Rise as OpenAI Relaxes GPT-5.6 Sol Limits
item.content:encoded:
How to maintain code quality standards with AI code and vibe coding — Optional

AI-generated code can quickly create technical debt if teams skip consistent review, so code quality checks need to happen early on pull requests and across repositories. The article argues for scoped, rule-based LLM reviews tuned to a team’s standards rather than generic prompts to tools like Claude or Cursor.

  • AI development tools have improved enough that developers are spending more time prompting requirements and doing functional testing while spending less time reviewing generated code.
  • The article warns that unchecked AI-generated changes can accumulate technical debt, causing bugs in unexpected places and slowing development after an initial period of high velocity.
  • The article says teams are using code quality tools on pull requests and full repositories to catch code debt early, track findings, and identify teams that may need more senior development support or higher standards.
  • Aikido’s Code Quality feature runs LLM checks on a per-rule basis and allows teams to fine-tune or add rules so findings better match their code style.
  • The article says Aikido benchmarks and tunes prompts using manually labeled code samples, aiming to avoid flagging grey-zone cases that could frustrate developers.

OpenAI temporarily relaxes GPT-5.6 Sol usage limits — Optional

OpenAI temporarily removed the five-hour GPT-5.6 Sol usage limit for Plus, Pro, and Business users and reset current usage after heavy demand from Codex and ChatGPT Work. The company says efficiency improvements should make the model consume less usage going forward, though it is not necessarily unlimited.

  • OpenAI is temporarily removing the five-hour usage limit restriction for Plus, Pro, and Business plans after demand for GPT-5.6 Sol surged over the past 48 hours.
  • OpenAI also issued a one-time usage reset for everyone, giving users more room to use GPT-5.6 Sol for coding and agentic work.
  • Codex and ChatGPT Work count local messages and cloud-based tasks against a shared usage limit.
  • OpenAI product lead Tibo said the company is rolling out changes to make GPT-5.6 Sol more efficient across the board, which should result in less usage being consumed.
  • The temporary removal of the five-hour restriction does not necessarily make GPT-5.6 Sol completely unlimited.
